Product page

Delta Memory Force is a small, single-window RAM and process monitor first built for Windows 98 through 2000. Version 3.1 doesn't rewrite it — it repackages the same 2004 engine into an installer that behaves properly on Windows 11.

What it does

One window, no dashboards to configure: free/total RAM, live CPU load, a running process list pulled straight from the system process table, and enough control to act on what you see.

  • Free RAM readout

    Live free-memory and total-memory figures in MB, refreshed continuously alongside a scrolling CPU-history graph.

  • CPU load meter

    A percentage readout backed by a rolling strip chart, so a spike shows its shape, not just its peak.

  • Process list & priority control

    Every running executable with full path, thread count, and priority class (Real Time / High / Normal / Idle) — with a one-click priority dial and a Terminate & Delete option for runaway processes.

  • Disk usage strip

    Total and free space on C:\, shown as a simple bar rather than a second application to open.

1999 → 2026

1999
First written in Visual Basic 6 by Paul Aurelian Gagniuc as a lightweight alternative to Task Manager, at a time when 32–64MB of RAM made every megabyte worth watching.
2004
Delta Memory Force 2.0 — the version this page is built on — reaches its last known native build, packaged with the classic VB6 Package & Deployment Wizard.
2026
Repackaged as 3.1: same executable, a modern single-file installer, and the full VB6 runtime bundled so it installs cleanly and self-registers on a fresh Windows 11 machine.
What "3.1" actually means: the monitoring engine itself is untouched — it's the original 1999–2004 VB6 binary. The version bump refers to the distribution package: a single installer that carries every dependency the app needs (MSVBVM60.DLL, MSCOMCTL.OCX, COMCAT.DLL, OLEAUT32.DLL, OLEPRO32.DLL, and the rest of the original runtime set), registers them the same way the original 2004 installer did, and adds a proper uninstaller. Nothing here claims to be a modern rewrite.

Windows 11 compatibility

The interface, the metrics, and the process controls behave exactly as they did in 2004. The only thing Windows 11 changes is what has to be installed alongside the app first.

ComponentWindows 11 status
Core application (g2.exe)Runs unmodified — 32-bit, no compatibility shim required
VB6 runtime (MSVBVM60.DLL)Not preinstalled on most Windows 11 images — bundled by the 3.1 installer
MSCOMCTL.OCX / COMCAT.DLL / OLE componentsLegacy shared components — bundled and re-registered by the installer
Process priority & terminate controlsUses standard Win32 APIs, unaffected by OS version
